question: A man goes to Lucknow from Kanpur at a speed of 72 km/hr and returns to Kanpur at speed of 90 km/hr, through the same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance covered is equal for both parts of the journey, the average speed formula is:

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 72 × 90) ÷ (72 + 90)

⇒ Average Speed = 12960 ÷ 162 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Kanpur to Lucknow (S₁) = 72 km/hr

Speed from Lucknow to Kanpur (S₂) = 90 km/hr

**Method: LCM Approach**

⇒ Let the distance between Kanpur and Lucknow be the LCM of the speeds 72 and 90.

⇒ LCM of 72 and 90 = 360

⇒ Let total distance one way = 360 km

⇒ Time taken for onward journey = 360 ÷ 72 = 5 hours

⇒ Time taken for return journey = 360 ÷ 90 = 4 hours

⇒ Total Distance for the entire journey = 360 + 360 = 720 km

⇒ Total Time taken = 5 + 4 = 9 hours

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 720 ÷ 9 = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a person covers three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

When different distances are covered, the average speed is always calculated as Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, it is |S₁ − S₂|.
